United States example rates, around 2000

Source: R/data.R
usa_2000.Rd

Published U.S. demographic rates from around 2000, prepared as input tables for Hammel's process constructors. All rates are per person-year, and ages are in years, with half-open bands [age_start, age_end). Each source is a U.S. federal statistical publication. Source files, preparation scripts and further notes are in the package repository under validation/data/usa_2000_2001/; data-raw/usa_2000.R builds the datasets.

Usage

usa_2000_mortality

usa_2000_fertility

usa_2000_fertility_union

usa_2000_marriage

usa_2000_migration

Format

Tibbles with numeric age_start, age_end and rate columns, plus:

usa_2000_mortality

44 rows; sex ("f" or "m").

usa_2000_fertility

6 rows; no other columns.

usa_2000_fertility_union

12 rows; union_type ("partnered" or "unpartnered").

usa_2000_marriage

12 rows; no other columns.

usa_2000_migration

132 rows; origin and destination regions, 12 directed pairs by 11 age bands.

An object of class tbl_df (inherits from tbl, data.frame) with 6 rows and 3 columns.

An object of class tbl_df (inherits from tbl, data.frame) with 12 rows and 4 columns.

An object of class tbl_df (inherits from tbl, data.frame) with 12 rows and 3 columns.

An object of class tbl_df (inherits from tbl, data.frame) with 132 rows and 5 columns.

Source

Mortality: Arias E, Curtin LR, Wei R, Anderson RN. U.S. decennial life tables for 1999-2001, United States life tables. National Vital Statistics Reports 57(1). National Center for Health Statistics; 2008. Tables 2 and 3. https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr57/nvsr57_01.pdf

Fertility: Hamilton BE, Sutton PD, Ventura SJ. Revised birth and fertility rates for the 1990s and new rates for Hispanic populations, 2000 and 2001: United States. National Vital Statistics Reports 51(12). National Center for Health Statistics; 2003. Tables 1, 7 and 8. https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr51/nvsr51_12.pdf

Marriage: Kreider RM. Number, timing, and duration of marriages and divorces: 2001. Current Population Reports P70-97. U.S. Census Bureau; 2005. Supplemental Table 2. https://www.census.gov/library/publications/2005/demo/p70-097.html

Migration: Schachter J. Geographical mobility: March 1999 to March 2000. Current Population Reports P20-538. U.S. Census Bureau; 2001. Figure 3 and Tables B and D.

Mortality

usa_2000_mortality gives death rates by sex for ages 0-1, 1-5, five-year bands to 100, and an open 100+ band, for use with mortality(). Rates are abridged from the single-year U.S. decennial life tables for 1999-2001 as life-table deaths divided by person-years lived in each band (l100 / T100 for 100+). Under Hammel's constant hazards within bands, calculate_life_table() gives life expectancy at birth of 74.05 years for men and 79.38 for women, against the source's 74.13 and 79.47.

Fertility

usa_2000_fertility gives all-women birth rates for 2000 in five-year bands from 15 to 45, for use with fertility(). The published 10-14 and 45-49 rates are omitted, so the schedule sums to 2.049 births per woman rather than the published total fertility rate of 2.056.

usa_2000_fertility_union gives the same bands by union_type, mapping legally married women to "partnered" and unmarried women to "unpartnered". Legal marital status does not distinguish cohabitation. The 40-45 rates divide births to women 40 and older by women 40-44.

Marriage

usa_2000_marriage gives female marriage rates in five-year bands from 15 to 70 and an open 70+ band, for rate-based initiation in union_formation(). They are the published annual proportions of unmarried women who married in the year before a 2001 survey, used directly as search rates per person-year without conversion to hazards. Marriages include first marriages and remarriages. Search attempts can fail to find a partner, so simulated marriage rates need not match these.

Migration

usa_2000_migration gives approximate migration rates between the four census regions ("NE" Northeast, "MW" Midwest, "S" South, "W" West) by age, March 1999 to March 2000, for group_transition() on a region dimension with these categories. Each origin-destination rate is the all-ages flow divided by the origin's Census 2000 population, scaled by the national age pattern of interstate moves. The same age pattern is applied to every pair, which understates older-age moves to the South. The rates apply to individuals; see household() for moving family members together.
